Mockup · round 4 · 2026-10-23

Object Paint

Every show object already carries a Paint in its meta (record 0006). It is a screen colour written #rrggbb; none means the pool type's own colour (records 0144 and 0205). Today you type it as hex and it only shows in pool cells. This round proposes a picker, words for colours, painting many objects at once, and the places paint shows. Every mock is drawn by LumaCore's own kit.

1 · The picker

Three modes. Palette: 12 hues in four tones plus greys, the base hues named. Free: any colour. Theme: a link to one of the theme's paint slots (Dimmer, Position, Color … Special 1–4). A Theme paint is written Set Group 3 "Paint" Theme "Position"; it follows each viewer's own theme and changes everywhere when the slot changes in the theme editor. The Examples switch shows the colour in every place it appears. It opens on the mode you used last.

The theme editor: a Paint tab

The slots live in your profile's theme, beside the 14 UI colours but separate from them. Each starts at LumaCore's standard colour (the feature-group colours of the built-in templates), and you can change it, add your own and reset to LumaCore. Here Position was changed: everything painted Theme "Position" (objects, tags and the Position feature group) follows.

Feature groups and their rules

A feature group's colour defaults to the theme slot with its name, so the encoder bar, the preset pool and anything tagged Position share one colour. A feature group can still have its own Paint. The rules that place each attribute in a feature group (AttributeRule, first match wins, learned rules beat the standard table) can only be typed or listed as text today. Proposal: a Rules window: the rules in order (drag to reorder), each one's pattern and feature group, and a field that tells which rule places an attribute.

2 · Where paint shows

Pool cells already show it. These are the other places it could show; question 4 asks which ones.

Pools (built)

The Tree window and NAV tree: a swatch

Lists (<luma-grid>): the row tinted (chosen)

The Device Sheet: the fixture's paint on its name

3 · Colour from tags, Paint as the override

A tag has a Paint and a Priority. An object shows its own Paint if it has one; otherwise the colour of its painted tag with the highest Priority (equal priorities: the tag first in the tag tree); otherwise its pool's colour. Tag your position presets "Position" and they all take the position colour; give one preset its own Paint and it stands out. The inspector and the lists say where a colour comes from.

Lines: Set Tag "Position" "Paint" Blue · Set Tag "Position" "Priority" 20 · Set Preset 6 "Paint" Red (the override) · Set Preset 6 "Paint" none (back to its tags).

4 · Painting many

Painting a selection is one line (the range rule). A gradient across the selection and "by fixture type" are options for later.

Clean-ups that come with it

  • One colour parser for every Paint (today there are separate ones for objects, tags and feature groups, plus users and window settings).
  • The settings dialog's Theme button sends a value that object Paint refuses, and an empty Paint reads "Theme"; for objects it becomes none · the pool's colour.
  • Feature groups still set their colour with the old word Color as text; they move to Paint like everything else.
  • The pool cell sends each object's icon, but the pool never draws it; it could be drawn beside the paint.

Paint stays on each object's meta (record 0205): no appearance pool, and no colours kept only in a client.
